name: Deep cryogenic treatment of quenched X210CrW12 (AISI D3-type) cold-work tool steel at -180 C for 12-36 h with 2 C/min cooling and heating, followed by 300 C tempering
plain_name: Deep-freeze a chromium cold-work tool steel at -180 C for up to a day and a half so it wears more slowly
description: Quenched X210CrW12 tool steel (austenitised 920 C, 25 min) is cooled at 2 C/min to -180 C, held 12, 18, 24 or 36 h, warmed at 2 C/min and tempered at 300 C for 2 h; hardness, tensile strength and pin-on-disc wear are compared with conventional quench-and-temper. The cryogenic device appears only as a schematic/photo (model not named).
keywords: Deep-freeze a chromium cold-work tool steel at -180 C for up to a day and a half so it wears more slowly

sources.citation: Impact of Deep Cryogenic Treatment on X210CrW12 Steel's Wear Behavior and Microstructural Characteristics (Ozbek & Altan Ozbek, Materials 2025, 18(4):879), doi:10.3390/ma18040879

requirements.rationale: The sample space must hold -180 C (93.15 K) during the soak.
The longest treatment of the series holds the steel at -180 C for 36 h, so the machine must sustain an uninterrupted 36 h soak.
Cooling to the soak temperature is ramped at a controlled 2 C/min (programmable ramp, not plunge immersion).
Warming back from -180 C is also ramped at 2 C/min.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
